visual.detailed_description: Panel A (lung window) and panel B (soft-tissue window) show the same axial slice through the upper chest with an irregular soft-tissue-density region and a central black air-filled cavity in the upper lung on the left of the image. The opposite lung is aerated and the trachea is near the midline. Printed text is limited to panel letters A and B and a small letter P.

panels.general_description: Axial chest CT in a lung window showing a large cavitary lesion in the right upper lung.
panels.detailed_description: Axial chest CT in a lung window, shown in grayscale with the printed letter A at the top left. The left side of the image has a large, irregular soft-tissue-density region in the upper lung that abuts the mediastinum and chest wall. It contains an irregular, black air-filled cavity with a smooth-looking lumen at its center, and its margins are lobulated with patchy, mottled gray areas along the upper and medial edges. Scattered thin lines extend into the adjacent aerated lung. The opposite lung is aerated with normal-looking fine vessels. The trachea is a round black lumen near the midline, anterior to the vertebral body. A small yellow letter P is printed at the bottom center. Thin curved lines (cables) are visible outside the body at the top and the CT table lines at the bottom.

A white rectangular bar containing a small letter P is printed at the bottom center, and thin cables are visible above the shoulders.
